fixed_protocol.question: Can explicit deterministic repair retain repeatability across process counts, with useful speed and shared-RAM tradeoffs?

fixed.optional_reduce: same binary, flips enabled in Reduce route
fixed.model: strict FP32 pLDDT, existing AOT/native writer

screen.capture: full-float repair and hydrogen arrays, identities, PDBs and actual OpenMM Context properties

fixed_protocol.adaptive: If CUDA deterministic forces does not remove repair variants, test explicit single-thread CPU repair as a separately labelled backend; do not silently switch. If it passes, test the eight distinct public targets, both hydrogen routes, serial/eight-worker, with two interleaved fresh repetitions.
fixed_protocol.memory: 20 ms MemAvailable; 5 s pre, 8 s post; peak additional RAM and pre/post baseline sensitivity; 0.25 GiB drift flag; no RSS or CUDA sums.
fixed_protocol.acceptance: Report exactness within and between conditions separately. Preserve all original atoms, protonation, topology, finite coordinates and audit failures. No change enabled on main/dev; user review required.

screen2.reason: CUDA single DeterministicForces=true still varied in concurrent repairs
screen2.cpu_hydrogens: unchanged CPU1 default force setting; only repair altered

validation_correction.reason: The comparison validator wrongly forbade Reduce side-chain flips already allowed by the frozen protocol. Production code and chemistry completed successfully and are unchanged.
validation_correction.reuse: Five completed conditions retained without repetition. Only the failed-validation case is repeated because its complete-container duration was not durably recorded.
